correctness.rationale: For every edge set F, an undominated edge has both endpoints of selected degree zero. Since a windmill consists of a hub and disjoint rim cliques, this yields precisely the two hub cases used in a disjoint inclusion–exclusion count. In the hub-covered case, each blade can have at most one zero-degree rim vertex, so T_m^(1) minus all-spoke-free T_m^(0) counts exactly the selected-spoke configurations. In the hub-uncovered case every rim vertex needs an internal selected edge, counted by A_m. The minimum proof uses the sharp efficiency of internal edges versus spokes, with mutually exclusive local P/E/Q and t/u equality classifications; no finite scan is treated as an infinite proof. Independent incidence-bitmask brute enumeration on 58 tuples and 572252 edge subsets matches every polynomial coefficient, plus exact closed minimum counts and broader algebraic coefficient tests.

value.rationale: Edge domination and its all-cardinality counting problem are natural NP-hard graph tasks; a nonhomogeneous one-hub clique union provides a motivated infinite family. The three-product hub-correction identity computes every coefficient by per-blade finite sums rather than full edge-subset enumeration. The sharp parity change from L to L+1, exact minimum-family multiplicities, and distinction between matching and nonmatching optimal sets are additional structural information, providing usable benchmark formulas beyond the already known scalar friendship case. This is not an arbitrary numerical slice or a mere lower-bound increment.
